what: the worker's hot paths profiled under real load: a real worker_main process (8 actors, one queue, max_concurrency=8) draining continuously-enqueued non-batch jobs, sampled in-process (cProfile, tracemalloc) and from outside (py-spy, pg_stat_statements, pg_locks)
harness: benchmarks/hotpath_load.py (roles: worker / client / orchestrate; --slot-pool for the transactional shape)

workload.shape: autonomous consume (no LOOP-connection registration), non-batch enqueue

sustained_throughput_jps.note: interleaved 3x3 vs the fixed tree; medians within run noise, see fixes[0].throughput_note

top_inclusive.frame: structlog/stdlib.py:286 _proxy_to_logger (the logging path: log_state_change 19.7%, 2 state-change INFO lines/job + dispatch lines)
worker/_bootstrap.py:2604 _guarded (the sibling-lifetime wrapper; inclusive = the loops' own time)

top_exclusive.frame: asyncio/base_events.py:476 create_task (the two loops' wait-racing task churn)

py_spy_during_drain.verdict: on-CPU under load is dominated by the logging pipeline (~23%, a byte-contract, not touched), the asyncio event loop, and asyncpg; taskq's own per-job code is thin (dispatch_one_job self ~84 us/job)

cprofile.note: CPython 3.13's profiler double-counts coroutine ncalls (verified: exactly 1 dispatch_one_job per job by a runtime counter); relative self-times hold

statements_per_job.pool_release_reset_statements: CLOSE ALL; pg_advisory_unlock_all(); UNLISTEN *; RESET ALL (one round trip, 4 statements counted)
statements_per_job.verdict: the single biggest statement family is asyncpg's pool-release reset (library behavior; removing it would drop the release-reset safety net - a behavior change, documented not fixed). taskq's own writes are 1.26 statements/job.

slot_pool_shape.verdict: the SAVEPOINT _tq_actor pair is the transactional path's deliberate per-job integrity machinery (a mid-body failure rolls to savepoint, the tx survives), not a redundancy

per_tick_allocations.method: tracemalloc snapshots 4000 jobs apart inside the real worker process
per_tick_allocations.verdict: the per-job path is allocation-neutral: no leak, the per-claim dicts are freed within the cycle

lock_contention.method: pg_locks (NOT granted) + pg_stat_activity wait_event sampling at 250 ms during the drain
lock_contention.verdict: no DB-side contention in the dispatch path at this scale

idle_polling.verdict: an idle leader worker is NOT silent: the leader loops' 1 s cadences are settings-driven defaults (behavior), but the per-tick SQL re-render INSIDE them was code - fixed (see fixes[0])

insights_n_plus_1.verdict: NOT fixed: the six aggregates dominate the page cost; asyncpg cannot pipeline distinct parameterized statements on one connection (InterfaceError), and gathering across pool connections would break the route's one-checkout snapshot discipline. Pipelining would be a speculative optimization.

fixes.name: the sweep statements' per-call SQL re-render
fixes.where: src/taskq/backend/_sweeps.py (_render_sweep_sql + _render_event_ttl_base_sql, lru_cache 64), src/taskq/backend/postgres.py (heartbeat SQL rendered at backend init)
fixes.why: sweep_scheduled_to_pending runs on the leader's ~1 s scheduled-wake tick and re-rendered a 19,793-char template (plus 2 more) per call, byte-identical every time
fixes.red_green: benchmarks/ab_sweep_sql_render.py + benchmarks/results/hotpath-fix-sweep-render.json: direct render 1242 ns/call vs cached 70 ns/call (17.8x), byte-equality asserted per (template, schema), invalid-identifier ValueError unchanged per call
fixes.throughput_note: the e2e drain is unchanged within run noise (base median 298 vs after 287 jps, interleaved 3x3) - expected: the fix removes the leader's per-tick render churn, not per-job work; the conservation pins (statement shape per job) are identical before/after
